newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt adjourns anti-corruption trial to May.
newsitem.headline: Egypt adjourns anti-corruption trial to May.

text.p: An Egyptian court has adjourned until May 11 the high-profile trial of a former public sector boss charged with taking millions of dollars in commissions, security sources said on Thursday.

They said Abdelwahhab el-Habbak, ex-chairman of the Holding Company for Engineering Industries, denied charges that he had appropriated 91 million pounds ($27 million) by illegal means during his 11 year career with the public firm. Habbak retired last May.
The court, which held its first session on Wednesday, heard the defence team, refused bail for Habbak, reinstated a travel ban and then adjourned the trial, the sources said.

Habbak has made headlines in Egypt since he was detained for questioning by the anti-corruption squad in September. Popular satirists Mostafa Hussein and Ahmed Ragab even ran a series of cartoons on the "Habbak School for Embezzlement".
In September, Habbak reportedly offered to repay the government $19 million he had deposited in Swiss bank accounts.
The Holding Company for Engineering Industries is parent company to 21 state manufacturing firms, several of which are listed for early privatisation.
